subjective: Pet parent reports that Golu is very manipulative and energetic, especially when his belongings are taken away. He exhibits playful, zooming behavior and puts things down one by one. This is Golu's first rabies vaccination. No previous rabies vaccines were given. No swelling or warmth was observed in the last 48 hours. Stool is normal. The pet parent usually feeds pumpkin daily and bananas twice a day to help with leg strength, but bananas were not given this week due to unavailability. After two days of banana feeding previously, Golu showed improvement.
objective: Golu's temperature is 100.7°F, which is within normal limits. No signs of swelling or warmth were observed in the last 48 hours. No abnormalities reported in stool. No physical examination details beyond temperature and absence of swelling were provided. No pulse measurement data available.
assessment: Golu is a young male Labrador Retriever receiving his first rabies vaccination. No adverse reactions such as swelling or warmth have been observed post-vaccination. The pet parent notes improved leg condition with banana supplementation. No current clinical abnormalities noted.
plan: Complete the rabies vaccination series with the final dose scheduled approximately 21 days after the first vaccination, likely next month. Continue dietary supplementation with pumpkin daily and bananas twice a day when available to support leg strength. Avoid bananas this week as per current feeding. Monitor for any adverse reactions post-vaccination such as swelling or warmth. Owner to avoid allowing Golu to bite or be aggressive with belongings. No additional diagnostics or treatments indicated at this time.
conclusion: Golu, a young male Labrador Retriever, is undergoing his first rabies vaccination with no adverse reactions reported. The pet parent describes playful and manipulative behavior but no clinical concerns. Temperature and stool are normal. Dietary management includes pumpkin daily and bananas twice a day to support leg strength, with bananas withheld this week. The rabies vaccination series will be completed with a final dose in approximately 21 days. Owner instructions include monitoring for vaccine reactions and managing behavior to prevent biting.
